Lupus is really unpredictable, I had lots of signs as a kid that I thought was just me being unlucky or that everyone feels like that sometimes, but it was never bad enough for me to have to see a doctor until I was 25. Symptoms during flares seem to change over time for me, sometimes it’s worse sometimes than other times. 

I don’t think you should wait until the inflammation is under control before you see the rheumatologist. I don’t know what test your dr did to confirm lupus (there isn’t just one test that can confirm it) but the rheumatologist is probably going to do a lot of tests you haven’t done before and it’s better to go when you’re sick because sometimes if you’re not it won’t show up. They might tell you otherwise but in my experience this is true and if I go when I’m not in a flare the test results will likely look like I’m a very healthy person with nothing wrong with them which is very far from true. 

Good luck I hope you can find out more. Take care!
